# ui::ClassicPalette

Header: `winui/ui/themes/ClassicPalette.hpp`.

The classic era's color scheme: the colors a classic 3-D look is drawn with. [Palette](palette.md) is the Fluent counterpart.

[Theme::classic()](theme.md#classic) derives a whole [Theme](theme.md), every control's visuals included, from one of these. A Windows 95, 98 or 2000 look, Windows Classic on XP, or a custom scheme is one literal plus that derivation, with no hand-assembled [`ButtonVisual`](button-visual.md)s. [`face_text`](#face_text), [`window_text`](#window_text) and [`menu_text`](#menu_text) are separate fields, so a scheme with a dark face, such as classic "Eggplant", can use light text.

Example: 
```cpp
// A shipped scheme:
window.pin_theme(ui::Theme::classic(ui::ClassicPalette::windows_standard(),
                                        /*hot_track=*/false, "Microsoft Sans Serif"));

// A user-authored one, derived from its face and then touched up:
ui::ClassicPalette scheme = ui::ClassicPalette::from_face(ui::Color::from_rgba(128, 128, 64));
scheme.selection = ui::Color::from_rgba(128, 0, 128);
window.pin_theme(ui::Theme::classic(scheme, /*hot_track=*/true, "Microsoft Sans Serif"));
```

## bevel

```cpp
std::optional<ClassicBevelRamp> bevel {}
```

The bevel ramp, when the scheme states its own. nullopt, the default, derives it from [`face`](#face) with [classic_bevel_ramp_from_face()](namespace-ui.md#classic_bevel_ramp_from_face). High-contrast schemes need this: High Contrast Black pairs a black face with a white outer dark ring and gray inner rings, which no lightening or darkening of black produces.

## caption

```cpp
std::optional<ClassicCaption> caption {}
```

The caption and border colors, when the scheme states them. nullopt, the default, derives them as Windows 95 and 98's Windows Standard has them. The active caption is [`selection`](#selection) and an inactive one is the bevel ramp's `shadow`, both without a gradient. The active title is [`selection_text`](#selection_text), an inactive title is [`face`](#face), and both borders are [`face`](#face).

## windows_standard

```cpp
static ClassicPalette windows_standard()
```

The default "Windows Standard" scheme as Windows 95 and Windows 98 SE ship it: a `0xC0C0C0` face and a navy `0x000080` selection. The two versions use the same colors.

## windows_standard_2000

```cpp
static ClassicPalette windows_standard_2000()
```

"Windows Standard" as Windows 2000 and XP's Classic scheme ship it: the warmer `0xD4D0C8` face, a `0x0A246A` selection, a `0x000080` hyperlink, the flatter bevel ramp and a gradient caption. Combining parts of it with [windows_standard()](#windows_standard) gives a look no Windows version had.

## high_contrast_black_98

```cpp
static ClassicPalette high_contrast_black_98()
```

High Contrast Black as Windows 98 SE ships it. White on black, a purple `#800080` selection, green `#00FF00` disabled text, a pinkish `#D0B0B8` outer light bevel ring and pure-blue `#0000FF` hyperlinks. The last two look odd but are the shipped values.

## high_contrast_black_2000

```cpp
static ClassicPalette high_contrast_black_2000()
```

High Contrast Black as Windows 2000 and XP ship it, the scheme both switch to when high contrast is turned on. It is the Windows 98 scheme with a white outer light bevel ring, purple hyperlinks and white-on-black tooltips.

## monochrome_3x

```cpp
static ClassicPalette monochrome_3x()
```

Monochrome, the Windows 3.1 scheme closest to high contrast: black on white, silver buttons, a black selection and title bar. Windows 3.1 has no tooltip or hyperlink color, so tooltips and hyperlinks use the window colors. Pass it to [`Theme::classic(..., /*win3x_edge=*/true)`](theme.md#classic) for the Windows 3.x edges.

## from_face

```cpp
static ClassicPalette from_face(const Color& face)
```

A custom scheme derived from [`face`](#face). The bevel comes from [classic_bevel_ramp_from_face()](namespace-ui.md#classic_bevel_ramp_from_face), and the rest takes the colors every classic scheme shares: a white window, a navy selection, black text and the pale yellow tooltip. "Windows 95 with the Eggplant scheme" is `ClassicPalette::from_face(eggplant_face)`.
